data.title: Cirrus Breaks Ground on New Engine Run-Up Center
data.description:
Cirrus Breaks Ground on New Engine Run-Up Center

The 15,000-square-foot Engine Run-Up Center creates a state-of-the-art facility to test SR Series and Vision Jet engines and fuel calibration before aircraft certification and delivery

Key Highlights:

  • Cirrus started construction on the 15,000-square-foot Engine Run-Up Center in Duluth.
  • The facility will provide a centralized, climate-controlled environment year-round to safely and efficiently test SR Series, Vision Jet®, and TRAC10 aircraft engine systems and fuel calibration.
  • Cirrus will invest over $8 million in the Engine Run-Up Center.
  • The Engine Run-Up Center is expected to open in summer 2027.

Cirrus (Cirrus Aircraft Ltd.), the global leader in Personal Aviation™, broke ground on the 15,000-square-foot Engine Run-Up Center, designed to safely and efficiently test SR Series, Vision Jet®, and TRAC10 engine system functionality, performance, and fuel calibration as part of the aircraft certification process. Cirrus will invest over $8 million in the facility, which will provide a centralized, enclosed, well-equipped, climate-controlled building year-round. The Run-Up Center is expected to be completed and operational in summer 2027.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261023174589/en/

Cirrus broke ground on its new 15,000-square-foot Engine Run-Up Center, an investment of over $8 million that will enhance aircraft engine and fuel calibration testing efficiency for the SR Series, Vision Jet, and TRAC10. The climate-controlled facility is expected to be operational by summer 2027.

The new facility will feature two calibration stalls where Cirrus technicians can set up, test and adjust engines during operation. A separate, safe, climate-controlled control room will support data analysis and remote adjustments. Air-handling equipment, including an eight-foot exhaust collector, will ventilate the stalls, while sound-control measures will reduce airport noise.

Fuel calibration will be supported by two additional stalls designed specifically for fueling and defueling aircraft. Technicians set and adjust fuel systems in a space designed for flammable fluids, with fire protection and under flammable fluid handling requirements.

“The Engine Run-Up Center represents another significant investment in Cirrus’ manufacturing capabilities and our commitment to operational excellence,” said Zean Nielsen, Chief Executive Officer of Cirrus. “Engine run-ups and fuel system calibration are essential processes across aircraft manufacturing. This modern facility will allow us to streamline these critical operations, improve efficiency, and provide our team members with a dedicated environment to perform this work. As we continue to grow, investments like these strengthen our manufacturing infrastructure and position Cirrus to meet customer demand while maintaining high standards of quality and safety.”

“The new Engine Run-Up Center expands Cirrus’ footprint of more than 1.3 million square feet, much of it in Duluth, where we have produced more than 12,000 SR Series and Vision Jet aircraft,” said Patrick Waddick, President of Innovation & Operations of Cirrus. “For decades, we have challenged conventions through innovations that have transformed personal aviation and elevated customer experience. This facility continues that tradition by providing a modern, purpose-built environment that enhances safety, supports a world-class employee experience and helps us deliver the quality, precision, and innovation our customers expect from Cirrus.”

Cirrus manufactures the SR Series, the world’s best-selling high-performance single-engine piston aircraft, and the Vision Jet, the world’s best-selling jet in General Aviation. The company recently announced the TRAC10, a purpose-built aircraft powered by a FADEC engine for professional flight schools. Cirrus aircraft are renowned for their innovative safety systems – the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System® (CAPS®) and Safe Return™ Emergency Autoland.

To learn more about Cirrus, visit www.cirrusaircraft.com.

About Cirrus

Cirrus is the recognized global leader in personal aviation and the maker of the best-selling SR Series piston aircraft and the Vision Jet, the world’s first single-engine Personal Jet, and the recipient of the Robert J. Collier Trophy. Founded in 1984, the company has redefined aviation performance, comfort and safety with innovations like the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS) – the first FAA-certified whole-airframe parachute safety system included as standard equipment on an aircraft. To date, worldwide flight time on Cirrus aircraft is over 19 million hours, and over 300 people have returned home safely to their families as a result of the inclusion of CAPS as a standard feature on all Cirrus aircraft. The company has seven locations in the United States, including Duluth, Minnesota; Grand Forks, North Dakota; Greater Dallas, Texas; Greater Phoenix, Arizona; Greater Orlando, Florida; Knoxville, Tennessee and Benton Harbor, Michigan. Learn more at cirrusaircraft.com.

Nadia Haidar
PR Manager, Cirrus

data.title: Solar Energy Expert John Hrudicka Explains How Solar Battery Backup Supports Home Energy Security in HelloNation
data.description:
Solar Energy Expert John Hrudicka Explains How Solar Battery Backup Supports Home Energy Security in HelloNation

Solar Energy Expert John Hrudicka Explains How Solar Battery Backup Supports Home Energy Security in HelloNation

PR Newswire

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 23, 2026

The article explains how solar energy and battery storage can provide backup power for important household needs when the electrical grid is unavailable.

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How can solar and battery backup support home energy security? A recent HelloNation article featuring insights from John Hrudicka of Renew Solar Solutions in Nashville, Tennessee, explains how a properly designed solar and battery system can provide stored energy for important household needs during a power outage.

The article explains that solar panels alone do not necessarily provide electricity when grid power goes down. Most standard grid-connected solar systems shut down during an outage as a safety measure that prevents electricity from being sent onto power lines while utility crews may be making repairs. Homeowners who want backup power generally need battery storage as part of their system.

According to the article, a properly designed solar and battery system can generate electricity, store energy at the home, and provide backup power when the grid is unavailable. Stored energy can be directed to selected parts of the house, giving homeowners another source of electricity until utility service is restored.

Determining which household needs should remain powered is an important part of planning for home energy security. Refrigerators, lights, internet equipment, security systems, and selected outlets may be priorities for some homeowners, while others may want to include heating, cooling, or larger appliances. These choices can significantly affect the amount of battery storage required.

The article emphasizes that battery capacity must be matched with household energy needs and available solar production. Every battery can store a limited amount of energy, and operating larger appliances or more equipment will use that stored energy more quickly. Prioritizing essential electrical needs can help backup power last longer during an outage.

Solar production can also play an important role in extending backup power. During a daytime outage, solar panels may generate electricity that helps recharge battery storage. However, the article notes that solar battery backup does not provide unlimited electricity. Weather, season, shade, time of day, and nighttime conditions all influence how much solar energy is available.

The amount of time backup power lasts also varies from one household to another. Battery size and energy consumption both affect backup duration. A home using stored energy primarily for a refrigerator, lights, internet equipment, and a security system will have different requirements than a home attempting to power heating, cooling, or other large appliances.

The article recommends conducting an energy review before designing the system. A solar contractor can evaluate normal household energy use and discuss which equipment homeowners want to keep operating during an outage. This information can help determine the appropriate amount of battery storage for those priorities.

Homeowners are also encouraged to ask what a proposed solar and battery system will actually power during an outage and how long the battery may last based on expected energy use. Understanding how sunlight and solar production affect backup time can also help homeowners establish realistic expectations before installation.

The article further explains that home energy security does not necessarily require disconnecting from the utility grid. A home can remain connected during normal conditions while a solar and battery system provides an additional layer of protection when grid electricity becomes temporarily unavailable.

Battery storage can provide benefits outside of outages as well. Solar energy generated during the day can be stored for use later, giving homeowners greater flexibility in managing the electricity their solar panels produce.

The article concludes that solar battery backup is not intended to provide unlimited power or prevent outages from occurring. Instead, a properly planned system can provide another source of electricity when the grid goes down. By considering battery size, household energy use, available sunlight, and the equipment that matters most, homeowners can better understand how solar and battery backup can support home energy security.

How Solar and Battery Backup Support Home Energy Security features insights from John Hrudicka, Solar Energy Expert of Nashville, Tennessee, in HelloNation.

Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

data.title: Veraify Launches Token Management to Help Enterprises Master AI "Tokenomics"
data.description:
SUNNYVALE, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Veraify today added comprehensive token management capabilities to its AI-native security platform to help enterprises gain more visibility into their token usage and manage token costs. With Token Management, Veraify customers now get deeper insights into how, where, and who is consuming AI tokens and driving up AI costs. Unlike other token usage visibility tools in the market Veraify provides comprehensive support across all AI tools, whether or not the enterprise knows about or approves them, including Shadow AI and enterprise-approved tools in the same report.

AI tokens are the currency of the AI industry, determining how much AI usage costs each enterprise. As AI usage increases, AI bills have become a significant concern for CFOs. Goldman Sachs estimates that token consumption will multiply 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between 2026 and 2030. With multiple AI tools in use across the enterprise, including both approved and shadow AI, token costs can often come as an unwelcome surprise.

"AI Tokenomics is now a board-level issue. Every enterprise is wrestling with it," said Prakash Mana, CEO of Cloudbrink, the creator of Veraify. "AI has reached an inflection point, and executives are being asked to make adoption decisions without a clear view of the return. Visibility into token consumption is the foundation for measuring the ROI of AI. You can't manage AI ROI if you can't see your tokens. Veraify gives enterprises the visibility to adopt AI safely and decisively."

Veraify Token Management helps both functional leaders and CFOs to analyze their existing spend at a per-department level, per AI service level, and at user level. Veraify can provide token usage insights across Shadow AI, enterprise-approved AI, and different types of AI tools (native app, plugin, IDE/API/CLI and browser-based).

Veraify Token Management provides the following features and benefits:

  1. Token Usage across dimensions: Insights into token usage by enterprise-level, by department level, by user level, by AI service level and by individual model level. Benefit: Increase AI ROI. Understand how and where AI bills are going at multiple organizational levels.
  2. Single-pass AI Security + Token Management: Veraify's architecture allows the platform to enforce AI security guardrails (data protection, prompt injection prevention, etc.) as well as measure token usage in a single pass processing. Benefit: No impact to AI services performance.
  3. Comprehensive AI tool coverage: Monitors and measures AI service usage over a browser, as native app, as plugin or via APIs/IDEs. Benefit: Eliminate AI blind spots.
  4. Segregate Corporate vs Shadow AI bills: IT/AI teams can segregate the AI usage bills for corporate-approved AI services versus Shadow AI token usage bills. Benefit: Measure approved versus unapproved AI costs, and identify where to put future AI investments.
  5. Top Token Consumption: Quickly gauge the top token usage patterns (by users, by department, by AI service and model). Benefit: Prioritize AI cost optimization, including which areas to deep-dive and bring the AI costs under control.

Veraify Token Management builds on the platform's AI-native approach, adding AI token insights to endpoint intelligence, AI-aware policy enforcement, data protection, and secure high-performance connectivity all in one platform for AI governance, visibility, protection, and cost management.

Token Management is available immediately for Veraify customers. For more information about Veraify Token Management, go to https://veraify.ai/blog/cross-platform-ai-token-tracking/

About Veraify

Veraify from Cloudbrink is an AI-native secure access and governance platform that gives organizations the visibility, control, and protection required to safely adopt AI across the enterprise - securing AI usage, sensitive data movement, AI agents, and access to critical applications and infrastructure. Powered by Cloudbrink's industry-leading zero-trust architecture, Veraify combines full AI security, high-performance connectivity, distributed policy enforcement, and real-time visibility into an award-winning single platform designed for the AI era. For more information, visit Veraify.ai.

NEPTUNE CITY, NJ / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Nylabone⁠, an iconic brand in the Central Garden & Pet Company⁠ portfolio, has been named a 2026 Industry Icon in Consumer Products by The 2026 List⁠, presented by Industry & Influence⁠. The recognition highlights the brand's long-standing focus on helping dogs satisfy their natural urge to chew through product innovation, practical design, and solutions that encourage positive chewing habits.

Since 1955, Nylabone has been at the forefront of chew innovation, creating solutions that support healthy chewing for dogs at every stage of life. The brand starts with a behavior dogs naturally want to express, then develops chew toys that give it an appropriate outlet and help prevent destructive chewing, with options matched to different ages, sizes, and chewing strengths.

"As a veterinarian, I recommend providing dogs with appropriate chew toys to satisfy their natural urge to chew. Nylabone offers a variety of chew toys, including new Nylabone chew toys made with real meats for adult dogs and puppies, giving them an engaging and flavorful way to satisfy their natural chewing instinct," said Dr. Ruthanne MacPete, DVM, Nylabone Veterinary Partner.

Nylabone's latest innovation is its collection of chew toys made with real chicken, bison, venison, bacon, and beef⁠. Available in shapes including the Original Bone, Textured Ring, Femur Bone, and Comfort-Hold Wishbone, the U.S.-made collection combines flavor, durable materials, and textured designs that encourage engagement and help clean teeth as dogs chew.

Nylabone also helps pet parents choose the right chew. Packaging includes a chew meter and size recommendations, and usage instructions encourage matching products to a dog's age, weight, and chewing strength, supervising use, and replacing toys as they wear.

The 2026 List recognizes 100 Industry Icons across ten categories, highlighting companies, creators, and leaders for innovation, leadership, and industry impact. Nylabone's recognition connects its 70-year history with its continued evolution of a familiar consumer-product category.

Industry & Influence explores the brand's approach to product development and canine behavior in "Instinct to Innovation: How Nylabone has Enhanced the Chewing Experience for Dogs⁠."

Explore Nylabone's 2026 Industry Icon profile⁠. For product information, visit nylabone.com⁠.

Nylabone, a leader in healthy chewing since 1955, crafts high-quality chew toys, tasty chew treats, exciting play toys, and innovative dental solutions. A family-founded company, Nylabone has a history of helping pet parents take the best possible care of their dogs. They are committed to developing world-class solutions for destructive chewing, separation anxiety, dental health, and more, helping dogs live fuller, happier lives. Recommended by veterinarians, Nylabone® products encourage a positive relationship between humans and their furry best friends. To put it simply, Nylabone Chews Best™! For more information, visit www.nylabone.com⁠. Nylabone is a brand owned by TFH Publications, Inc., a subsidiary of California-based Central Garden & Pet Company and a leader in responsible animal care for over 70 years.

data.title: Volkswagen Agrees With Union to Start Job Cut Talks Next Month
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras 




  Automaker Volkswagen said it agreed with German union IG Metall to start negotiations around job and cost cuts at the end of next month. 



  The company, which houses a vast stable of brands that includes VW, Audi and Porsche, said Friday that talks are scheduled to begin on Nov. 24 and continue on Dec. 15 at its facilities in Emden and Zwickau, respectively. 



  "Given the sharp deterioration of the economic situation, Volkswagen's objective is to reduce labor costs as quickly as possible," it said, adding that the group intends to remain competitive and ensure its long-term viability. 



  Under the collective bargaining agreement of 2024, the parties committed to a reduction of more than 35,000 jobs at Volkswagen's German sites by 2030. The group's plan provides for an additional reduction of 12,000 positions at Volkswagen by 2030. 



  Volkswagen has been working on a broad cost-cutting plan that could see job cuts double and aims for billions of euros a year in cost savings as the company faces a number of challenges including fierce Chinese competition. 



  The carmaker employed more than 600,000 people at the end of 2025, according to the company's website. 





  Write to Andrea Figueras at andrea.figueras@wsj.com

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Decisions From Fed, Other Central Banks in Focus
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff 




  Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting October 26. 



  An interest-rate decision by the Federal Reserve will be the highlight of a busy week ahead. Rates are widely expected to be left on hold, but hikes are expected in future as data point to a robust U.S. economy. 



  Rate decisions are also due in Canada and the eurozone. The European Central Bank's decision comes amid budget uncertainty in France that has caused a spike in French borrowing costs, while the U.K. government's budget presentation will also attract attention. 



  In Asia-Pacific, central bank decisions in Japan, New Zealand and Thailand headline the economic calendar, alongside growth figures from South Korea and Taiwan, plus China's industrial profits and activity surveys. 





  U.S. 





  The U.S. Federal Reserve is set to announce an interest-rate decision on Wednesday, where it is widely expected to leave the Fed Funds rate on hold following September's increase. Rates are expected to rise again in the coming months but recent economic data and comments from Fed officials suggest there is no urgency to hike again for now. 



  "With heavy hitters, such as [Fed officials] Philip Jefferson, Michelle Bowman and Chris Waller suggesting that while they are likely to hike again, there is no pressing need to do it quite yet, markets and economists are united in expecting an 'on hold' decision," ING economist James Knightley said in a note. 



  Still, given evidence that the U.S. economy is growing strongly, the jobs market is healthy and inflation is high, a rate increase in December is likely, he said. 



  Investors will thus be watching out for any signals on the likely timing and pace of future rate increases. 



  "Investors will be looking for clues about whether persistent inflation and elevated energy prices could justify further tightening," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said in a note. 



  U.S. money markets priced only a 10% chance of a quarter-point rate hike on Wednesday but priced a high chance of an increase in December, LSEG data showed. Markets fully priced two rate hikes by April. 



  Advance third-quarter GDP data and September PCE inflation data--the Fed's preferred measure of inflation--are due on Thursday and could be key indicators for the rate outlook. 



  Other data include durable goods orders for September, the Conference Board's October consumer confidence index and September new home sales on Tuesday, followed by weekly jobless claims data on Thursday. 





  Canada 





  The Bank of Canada announces an interest-rate decision on Wednesday, with markets pricing an 81% chance of a 25 basis-point hike in the key rate to 2.50%. 



  HSBC analysts said recent survey data have suggested a rate hike is likely, notably a rise in long-term consumer inflation expectations, even as other hard economic data have been on the soft side. 



  Analysts at TD, however, said they don't share the markets' conviction that rates will rise, "given limited inflation breadth and uncertainty over the near-term outlook." 



  Canadian GDP data for August will be released Friday. 





  Eurozone 





  The European Central Bank announces a decision on Thursday, where it is widely expected to leave the deposit rate at 2.50% as policymakers take a pause after raising interest rates in September. 



  Recent economic data have suggested the region's economic outlook remains uncertain while a recent jump in sovereign-bond yields, particularly in France due to debt and budget concerns, will likely concern policymakers. 



  Investors will pay close attention to any signals from the press conference after the ECB's announcement on the prospect of further rate increases in the coming months. 



  "So far, there is no evidence of significant indirect or even second-round effects from the second energy shock on inflation. The recent increase of long-term yields provides some degree of additional tightening," Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note. 



  "Both factors remove the urgency from delivering another rate hike next week already. The December meeting appears the more natural moment to change the policy stance, in light of new data and updated projections," they said. 



  Also attracting attention will be provisional eurozone gross domestic product data for the third quarter plus provisional October inflation data from individual eurozone countries, including France and Germany, on Friday. 



  Other data include the German October Ifo survey on Monday; the German GfK consumer confidence survey for October on Wednesday; and eurozone business and consumer surveys on Thursday. 





  U.K. 





  Treasury Chief John Healey's presentation of the U.K. budget on Wednesday will be a key focus for U.K. investors. 



  U.K. public finances are tight, though the budget isn't expected to contain anything that would upset U.K. government bonds or sterling. 



  "This should be a dramafree affair, with difficult decisions on tax and spending kicked into the long grass," HSBC analysts said in a note. 



  Healey also appears to have "a little more room for maneuver than we had calculated, which should mean he is able to offer some small-scale temporary measures around the cost of living in the near term, without having to do too much tightening to restore headroom," they said. 



  The market is currently "well disposed to the U.K.," although that support isn't guaranteed. 



  "The budget needs to go well in the current nervy conditions. Too much additional issuance and anything that looks inflationary could harm the current positive sentiment," the analysts said. 



  U.K. mortgage and consumer lending for September are due on Thursday. 





  Sweden 





  Swedish gross domestic product data for the third quarter are due Thursday. 





  Japan 





  The Bank of Japan concludes a two-day policy meeting on Oct. 30 and is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 1.25%, putting the focus on guidance about its next increase. 



  "Based on the BOJ's recent communications, while there has been no change in its overall stance of continuing rate hikes, it has suggested that the next move is more likely to come at the December meeting" versus at the October meeting, J.P. Morgan economist Ayako Fujita said. 



  "A hold in October looks the most likely outcome, although there is a possibility of at least one hawkish dissenting vote," Fujita said. Investors will watch how the BOJ assesses underlying inflation and explains the timing of further tightening. 



  October consumer prices for Tokyo are due Friday morning, providing an early indication of nationwide inflation ahead of the decision. September industrial production, retail sales and unemployment figures are also scheduled for release. 



  The BOJ will buy government bonds Wednesday, targeting maturities of more than three years and up to 10 years, as well as inflation-indexed securities. The purchases could support the bond market ahead of the policy meeting. 



  The Ministry of Finance will auction about 2.8 trillion yen of two-year sovereign notes Thursday. Bidders may be cautious as they await the BOJ's decision and Gov. Kazuo Ueda's press conference the following day. 





  China 





  A gathering of China's top Communist Party officials will take center stage, alongside industrial profit figures and official activity surveys that will offer a fresh read on economic momentum. 



  The Fifth Plenary Session of the party's 20th Central Committee takes place in Beijing from Oct. 26 to 29. The focus will likely be political rather than economic, but markets will scrutinize the communique for new signals, ING economists said. 



  September industrial profits are due Tuesday, with ING watching whether August's slowdown deepened or began to reverse. The figures will shed light on earnings pressures facing industrial businesses and their capacity to invest. 



  Official manufacturing and nonmanufacturing purchasing managers indexes for October follow Saturday. Factory orders will offer clues to the strength of domestic and overseas demand, while the nonmanufacturing survey, covering services and construction, will show whether National Day holiday spending helped lift services activity. 





  Australia / New Zealand 





  Australian inflation data and a series of central-bank appearances will make the week pivotal for bond traders assessing the likelihood of another interest-rate increase. 



  The Reserve Bank of Australia has maintained a hawkish tone, recently warning that the inflation outlook has become "materially worse." Traders see a 50% probability of a further rate increase at its November meeting, a prospect that could strengthen if Wednesday's third-quarter inflation figures exceed expectations. 



  RBA Chief Economist Sarah Hunter and Deputy Gov. Andrew Hauser are scheduled to speak during the week, before senior officials appear before parliament Friday. The appearances will give policymakers ample opportunity to reinforce their concerns about inflation. 



  In New Zealand, the central bank is expected to raise interest rates by another 25 basis points to 3.0% on Wednesday. Although headline inflation cooled in the third quarter, underlying measures pointed to more persistent price pressures, economists said. 





  South Korea 





  The Bank of Korea releases third-quarter gross domestic product data Tuesday, with some analysts expecting growth to have accelerated on strong semiconductor exports and investment. 



  Nomura economist Jeong Woo Park forecasts growth of 1.6% from the previous quarter and 4.0% from a year earlier, sharply above his previous estimates of 0.1% and 2.4%, respectively. The economy expanded 0.6% on quarter and 3.7% on year in the second quarter. 



  Nomura has also raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.6% from 3.2%. 



  South Korea's chip-led expansion could keep annual growth at or above 3% over the next three years, Citigroup economist Jin-Wook Kim said in a recent note. He projects growth of 3.7% in 2026, 3.1% in 2027 and 3.0% in 2028. 



  (MORE TO FOLLOW) Dow Jones Newswires



  October 23, 2026 12:23 ET (16:23 GMT)

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hagens Berman, a prominent national trial law firm specializing in securities fraud and shareholder rights, alerts investors in Gildan Activewear Inc. (NYSE: GIL) to a class action lawsuit filed in federal court.

The firm encourages Gildan investors who purchased shares on the NYSE only and suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now.

  • Class Period: Feb. 19, 2025 – June 15, 2026

  • Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/gil 
  • Contact the Firm Now: GIL@hbsslaw.com
                                            844-916-0895

CASE ALLEGATIONS & TRIGGERING EVENTS:

The Gildan Activewear class action lawsuit alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made false and/or misleading statements regarding the company's financial condition, internal controls, and sales growth drivers.

Specifically, the complaint alleges Defendants concealed that:

  1. Gildan engaged in channel stuffing by overloading wholesalers and distributors with excess inventory to artificially inflate reported sales and organic growth metrics;
  2. The company's top-line revenue growth was driven by unsustainable inventory pull-forwards rather than genuine market share gains;
  3. Gildan's offering and M&A disclosures overstated projected synergies and growth prospects relating to its acquisition of HanesBrands while concealing peak Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and distributor saturation.

The Truth Emerges: On June 16, 2026, activist short-seller Jehoshaphat Research published a detailed investigative report titled "Stuffing All of the Channel Some of the Time?" detailing Gildan's alleged reliance on aggressive premature sales recognition and distributor channel saturation. Following this report, Gildan's stock price fell $11.62 per share, or 18.75%, closing at $50.35 on heavy trading volume.

WHAT GIL INVESTORS CAN DO?

If you suffered substantial losses purchasing or acquiring Gildan Activewear Inc. (NYSE: GIL) stock during the Class Period (February 19, 2025 – June 15, 2026), you may seek appointment as Lead Plaintiff for the class before the December 14, 2026 deadline.

  • Submit your losses now

"Our investigation is focused on whether Gildan may have engaged in improper sales and revenue recognition practices," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.

Whistleblowers: Persons with non-public information regarding Gildan should consider their options to help in the investigation or take advantage of the SEC Whistleblower program. Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. For more information, call Reed Kathrein at 844-916-0895 or email GIL@hbsslaw.com.

Hagens Berman, National Trial Attorneys, Encourages Bank of America (BAC) Investors With Substantial Losses To Contact Firm Prior To Dec. 15 Lead Plaintiff Deadline

Hagens Berman, National Trial Attorneys, Encourages Bank of America (BAC) Investors With Substantial Losses To Contact Firm Prior To Dec. 15 Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 23, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- National securities litigation law firm Hagens Berman alerts investors in Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) to a securities class action lawsuit filed in federal court against Bank of America and certain senior executives alleging violations of federal securities laws. The firm urges investors with substantial losses to submit their trading information.
  • Class Period: Aug. 1, 2025 – Oct. 13, 2026
  • Lead Plaintiff Deadline: Dec. 15, 2026
  • Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/bac 
  • Contact Email: BAC@hbsslaw.com 
  • Direct Firm Phone: 844-916-0895

Case Overview & Summary of Allegations

The securities class action lawsuit alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts regarding Bank of America's compliance controls and regulatory risk exposure. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose that:

  1. Deficient AML & BSA Compliance Controls: Bank of America maintained deficient Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) monitoring systems, underresourcing compliance functions in favor of revenue generation.
  2. Underreported Suspicious Transactions: The Bank failed to detect, track, or report over $5 billion in suspicious transactions to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), including over $1 billion tied to high-risk illicit finance.
  3. Regulatory & Financial Exposure: As a result of these failures, Bank of America faced immense regulatory enforcement actions and multi-billion-dollar penalties, making its prior statements regarding regulatory compliance, risk management, and internal controls materially false and misleading.

The Disclosure & Market Impact

On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury, FinCEN, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced landmark enforcement actions requiring Bank of America to pay over $1.2 billion in penalties for widespread BSA/AML failures and backlog issues.

Following this disclosure, Bank of America's stock price fell sharply by over 4.8%, closing at $51.39 per share on October 14, 2026, wiping out billions of dollars in market value and causing substantial damages to shareholders.

What Can BAC Investors Do?

If you purchased Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) shares during the Class Period (August 1, 2025 – October 13, 2026) and suffered losses, you may move the Court to serve as Lead Plaintiff no later than December 15, 2026. A Lead Plaintiff is a representative party acting on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation.

  • Submit your losses now 
  • Learn More: Visit www.hbsslaw.com or contact Reed Kathrein at (844) 916-0895 or via email at BAC@hbsslaw.com.

"We're focused on the apparent disparity between the bank's assurances and the Treasury's revelations," said Reed Kathrein, a Hagens Berman partner.

Whistleblowers: Persons with non-public information regarding Bank of America should consider their options to help in the investigation or take advantage of the SEC Whistleblower program. Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. For more information, call Reed Kathrein at 844-916-0895 or email BAC@hbsslaw.com.

About Hagens Berman
Hagens Berman is a global plaintiffs' rights complex litigation firm focusing on corporate accountability. The firm is home to a robust practice and represents investors as well as whistleblowers, workers, consumers and others in cases achieving real results for those harmed by corporate negligence and other wrongdoings. Hagens Berman's team has secured more than $2.9 billion in this area of law. More about the firm and its successes can be found at hbsslaw.com. Follow the firm for updates and news at @ClassActionLaw.

data.title: Sexual Assault Lawyer Philadelphia: David P. Thiruselvam of the Victims’ Recovery Law Center Fights for Survivors' Civil Rights
data.description:
PHILADELPHIA, PA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / David P. Thiruselvam, sexual assault lawyer in Philadelphia and founder of the Victims' Recovery Law Center, is reminding survivors of sexual violence throughout Philadelphia that their legal options extend far beyond the criminal justice system. As a Philadelphia sexual assault attorney, David P. Thiruselvam represents survivors in civil claims against perpetrators, institutions, employers and property owners, without requiring any police report, criminal prosecution or conviction.

For many survivors, the decision whether to report a sexual assault to law enforcement is deeply personal. Civil litigation removes that requirement. A civil claim for sexual assault in Philadelphia is filed by the survivor directly, is governed by a lower standard of proof than criminal court and can result in significant financial compensation for medical costs, therapy, lost income, pain and suffering and emotional distress. A rape victim lawyer in Philadelphia can pursue these claims regardless of whether criminal charges were ever filed.

The Victims' Recovery Law Center's civil practice for sexual assault survivors is built around a core principle: the perpetrator is often not the only party with legal responsibility. Institutions, employers, property owners and organizations whose negligence created the conditions for the assault can be named as defendants in a Philadelphia sexual assault civil case. These institutional defendants carry commercial liability insurance, making them the most viable path to meaningful financial recovery for survivors.

"Survivors of sexual violence in Philadelphia often feel that the civil justice system is closed to them if the criminal case fell apart," said David P. Thiruselvam. "As a sexual assault lawyer in Philadelphia, I want every survivor to know that the civil path is open regardless of what the criminal system did or did not do."

All consultations at the Victims' Recovery Law Center are confidential. The firm handles all sexual assault civil cases on a contingency fee basis, meaning survivors pay nothing unless the firm recovers compensation on their behalf.

About the Victims' Recovery Law Center

The Victims' Recovery Law Center, led by Philadelphia sexual assault attorney and shooting victim lawyer David P. Thiruselvam, is a Pennsylvania-based civil litigation firm dedicated exclusively to representing survivors of gun violence, sexual assault, rape, child abuse and other violent crimes. David P. Thiruselvam is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and is licensed in Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey. The firm serves clients throughout Philadelphia and the greater Pennsylvania area. Survivors can reach the firm at 215-546-1433 or victimrecoverylaw.com.

data.title: GA-ASI Partnering With Spirit Defense For FQ-42 CCA Production
data.description:
SAN DIEGO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), the world leader in Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), today is announcing our partnership with Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, to support airframe production of the new FQ-42 Vengeance Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA). In June, GA-ASI won a contract from the U.S. Air Force (USAF) to produce FQ-42. Spirit Defense's role as a fuselage design-build partner brings together the company's engineering and advanced manufacturing capabilities to support the program from design through production.

GA-ASI has been the sole manufacturer of its line of UAS - which includes MQ-9A Reaper®, MQ-1C Gray Eagle®, MQ-20 Avenger®, and MQ-9B SkyGuardian®/SeaGuardian - since the company's inception in 1992. For the FQ-42 program, partnering with Spirit Defense is a strength multiplier for the company and the nation, offering manufacturing capacity and industrial depth to scale CCA production faster, while strengthening production resilience, and reducing the risk of single points of failure.

"We're excited to be working with Spirit Defense," said GA-ASI President David R. Alexander. "We've established our proven design, development, and manufacturing capability for the FQ-42. With Spirit Defense we add capacity, which is exactly the kind of production resilience our U.S. Air Force customer is looking for with its CCA ramp-up. This kind of partnership represents the scalable industrial base the Air Force and the U.S. Department of War are looking for from industry."

"We're proud to bring deep manufacturing expertise and proven capabilities to this important program," said Keith Schrader, president and CEO of Spirit Defense. "Our team understands the responsibility that comes with supporting critical national defense programs, and we're ready to deliver for our customer and the warfighter."

FQ-42 is a purpose-built, uncrewed fighter, developed with USAF as part of ongoing investment in next-generation semi-autonomous combat aircraft. The jet's modular design enables rapid integration of mission systems and mission autonomy software. GA-ASI's software architecture, demonstrated through live flight tests on multiple airframes, provides the foundation for human-machine teaming in complex combat scenarios.

Potential CCA manufacturing partnerships don't end here. Around the world, GA-ASI is in discussions with numerous international militaries interested in our Gambit Series of modular CCAs. The Gambit Series is a family of uncrewed combat jets, derived from our work on FQ-42, XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station, and MQ-20 Avenger, and optimized for roles such as electronic warfare, suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), Destruction of Enemy Air Defenses (DEAD) and stand-off precision strike, making it a versatile option for evolving security needs.

Nations interested in procuring aircraft from the Gambit Series also have an opportunity to insert indigenous manufacturing into those programs, as well as integration of their own sensors, weapons and other combat technologies.

About Spirit Defense

Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, is an independent supplier to the defense industry. Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, the company provides engineering, design-build, manufacturing, and lifecycle support for defense programs. Leveraging more than a century of aircraft design and manufacturing experience, Spirit Defense helps customers move innovative concepts from development to production through rapid prototyping, scalable manufacturing, and proven aerospace expertise.

About GA-ASI

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc., is the world's foremost builder of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS). Logging more than 9 million flight hours, the Predator® line of UAS has flown for over 30 years and includes MQ-9A Reaper®, MQ-1C Gray Eagle®, MQ-20 Avenger®, MQ-9B SkyGuardian®/SeaGuardian®, XQ-67A, and FQ-42 Vengeance. The company is dedicated to providing long-endurance, multi-mission solutions that deliver persistent situational awareness and rapid strike.

For more information, visit www.ga-asi.com.
